Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA), Bengaluru, for the Government of Karnataka and the Directorate of Medical Education
https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/pget2026
MDS
MD/MS/Diploma (after MCC's announcement)
Government seats (G), including the Government share in private colleges
Private (GMP, OPN, minority) and Others (Q) seats
NRI seats (N)
In-service candidate under the Government / DME of Karnataka (detailed in-service guidelines will be published later)
Government
State-quota seats in government colleges, and the government's share of seats in private colleges.
GMP
Private-college seats for candidates under clause b or c (10 years of school in Karnataka).
OPN
Open private-college seats, filled on NEET All India merit, for any Indian citizen.
NRI
15% of seats in private colleges, for NRIs, their children or wards, PIOs, OCIs and foreign nationals.
Others (Q)
10% of seats in private colleges (5% in private universities), open to all qualified candidates except NRI, PIO, OCI and foreign national candidates.
Check which eligibility clause you fit

Before you apply, confirm you meet one of the eligibility clauses (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, y or z) on the KEA website. You enter its clause code in the application. The fee isn't refunded for any reason.
https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/pget2026
Create your profile online

Register on the KEA PGET 2026 portal with your NEET-PG 2026 or NEET-MDS 2026 roll number. Your name, parents' names, date of birth, NBE score and mobile number are fetched from NBE data. An OTP goes to the mobile number you registered with NBE. Don't share it.
https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/pget2026
Fill in the application

Applications are online only; offline or postal forms aren't accepted. Enter your eligibility clause code, reservation category, educational qualification and contact details. In-service candidates enter their in-service details. Upload your photograph, left thumb impression and signature.
Pay the registration fee
Pay online through the payment gateway: ₹750 for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD, ₹1,500 for General/2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹4,000 for non-Karnataka candidates and ₹7,000 for NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates.
Check, declare and print

Until you select the declaration, you can edit the form any number of times and take draft printouts. Once you declare, nothing can be changed. Take the final printout and keep your application ID and password private.
Get your documents verified at KEA

Clause a and clause y candidates don't need to attend, unless they claim NRI Ward or religious minority reservation. Everyone else books a slot on the KEA website and attends in person at KEA, 18th Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, with originals and two sets of photocopies. You get a documents verification slip, which you need to enter options. KEA has published these steps for PG Dental (NEET MDS); confirm the PG Medical arrangements with KEA.
Enter your options, then check the mock allotment

Enter your college and course options in order of priority. The same list is used for Rounds 1 and 2; the mop-up round needs fresh options. A mock allotment shows an indicative result. You can then add, delete or reorder options until the last date for real allotment.
Round 1: see your allotment and pick a choice
Log in after the Round 1 result and select one of four choices. If you don't select one, your seat is cancelled automatically and you can't take part in later rounds.
Pay, submit originals and join

Pay the fees, submit your original documents to KEA, collect the admission order and report to the college by the last date on it. Then update your joining status on the KEA portal and ask the college to enter your reporting details on its portal.
Later rounds
After Round 1 come Round 2, Round 3 (mop-up) and the stray vacancy round. KEA publishes the rules, instructions and schedule for each round on its website.
Qualified in NEET-PG 2026 or NEET-MDS 2026

Only candidates who scored at least the prescribed minimum in NEET-PG 2026 (MD/MS/Diploma) or NEET-MDS 2026 (MDS) can register. Qualifying alone doesn't give you a right to a seat. You must also meet the eligibility conditions and complete registration, including document verification.
NEET-MDS 2026 qualifying cut-offs

NBEMS cut-offs (out of 960): General/EWS 50th percentile, 308; General PwBD 45th percentile, 289; SC/ST/OBC (including their PwBD) 40th percentile, 271. Non-Karnataka candidates (including PwD) need the General (UR) 50th percentile: 308.
PG Medical rules take effect after MCC's announcement
This bulletin covers PG Medical and Dental, but its information about PG Medical comes into effect only after MCC announces it. Watch the KEA website for the PG Medical notice and schedule.
MDS: internship by 31st May 2026
For NEET-MDS 2026, the NBEMS cut-off date for completing your internship is 31st May 2026.
MD/MS/Diploma: internship cut-off as set by NMC/NBEMS
For NEET-PG 2026, the internship cut-off follows NMC/NBEMS. This bulletin doesn't state the date. A provisional internship completion certificate (Annexure 6) is accepted for the first round only.
Already hold a clinical PG degree
If you already hold a PG degree in any clinical specialty, you are not eligible for admission to any PG degree or diploma course.
MBBS/BDS in Karnataka with 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b)

You fit clause b: as on 31st March 2026 you studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in government or government-recognised institutions in Karnataka, passed SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there, and passed MBBS/BDS in Karnataka. A class you took more than one year to pass counts as one year. You're eligible for Government, GMP, OPN and Others (Q) seats, and minority seats if you qualify.
MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka with 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause c)

You fit clause c: you studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in Karnataka, passed SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there, and passed MBBS/BDS from a recognised institution in India outside Karnataka. A class you took more than one year to pass counts as one year. You're eligible for Government, GMP, OPN and Others (Q) seats, and minority seats if you qualify.
MBBS/BDS in Karnataka without 10 years of school there (clause a)

You fit clause a: an Indian citizen who passed MBBS/BDS in Karnataka. That makes you eligible for Government seats, OPN seats and Others (Q) seats. GMP seats and the Karnataka religious and linguistic minority seats need 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b/c), so they aren't open to you, though Christian or Muslim candidates may get religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates. If clause d (a parent in the All India Service, Karnataka cadre, posted outside the state) or clause f (years in New Delhi while your parent was an MP from Karnataka) lets you count years outside Karnataka, answer 'Yes, in Karnataka' to the 10-year question.
MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka without 10 years of school there (clause y)

Government seats need MBBS/BDS in Karnataka (clause a) or 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b/c), and GMP seats need clause b/c. As an Indian citizen who passed MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka, you can apply for OPN seats (open to all Indian citizens) and Others (Q) seats. If you're a Christian or Muslim candidate, religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates are offered may also come to you. If you qualify under clause d, e, f or g (see 'Other routes'), Government seats may be open to you too. Confirm with KEA.
MBBS/BDS from outside India

You must have passed the FMGE screening test, be registered with MCI/DCI (or a State Medical Council) and complete your internship by the prescribed date. Government seats appear to need MBBS/BDS from India (clause a or c), and Others (Q) seats need a college affiliated to a university in India, so only OPN seats and, if you qualify, NRI seats appear to be open. If you studied 10 years in Karnataka, clause c's table row (which only says MBBS/BDS 'from outside the State of Karnataka') could open Government and GMP seats too. Confirm with KEA.
NRI seats are for NRIs and their children or wards

NRI seats are for NRIs, children or wards of NRIs, PIOs, OCIs and foreign nationals. You told us no one is an NRI for your application, so NRI seats aren't open to you unless an NRI relative sponsors you as a ward (relationship as per the Supreme Court order in W.P.(c) No. 689/2017). Confirm with KEA.
NRI seats: sponsor documents needed

NRIs, children of NRIs and NRI wards can apply for NRI seats (15% of seats in KPCF, KRLMPCA, AMPCK and private university colleges). If you claim NRI Ward (as an NRI's child or ward), you need the Ward Certificate (Annexure 17), the sponsor's NRI/OCI status certificate from the Indian Consulate issued within the last 6 months (Annexure 17(A)), a family tree signed by a Tahsildar, and copies of the sponsor's bank passbook, passport and visa. Others (Q) seats aren't open to NRI, PIO, OCI or foreign national candidates: if you yourself are the NRI (not just your parents), don't count on Q seats. 'NRI' here means an individual resident outside India who is an Indian citizen or a PIO, including OCIs (Income Tax Act 1961, sections 115C(e) and 6).
OCI, PIO and foreign national candidates (clause z)

OCI, PIO, NRI and foreign national candidates apply under clause z. Government, GMP and OPN seats need Indian citizenship, and Others (Q) seats exclude NRI, PIO, OCI and foreign nationals, so only NRI seats are open to OCI and foreign national candidates.
Foreign nationals: registration

Your qualification must be registered with the registering authority of the country where you got your basic medical degree, and recognised by that country's medical council. Get a temporary registration certificate from MCI/DCI for the course, within one month of securing admission.
Reservation is for Karnataka candidates only

SC/ST/OBC reservation applies only to Karnataka SC/ST/OBC candidates. Non-Karnataka candidates aren't eligible for reservation, and must score at least the General (UR) qualifying cut-off (50th percentile) to register. The bulletin doesn't define 'Karnataka candidate'; we've used your domicile. Confirm with KEA.
EWS isn't mentioned in this bulletin
EWS appears only in the NBEMS qualifying cut-off table (General/EWS). The bulletin states no Karnataka EWS reservation or EWS registration fee. Confirm with KEA how EWS candidates are treated.
SC candidates: SCA, SCB or SCC certificate

Karnataka has internal reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCA, SCB and SCC). Get a caste certificate with your SCA, SCB or SCC group printed on it and enter its RD number when you apply. Otherwise you can't select seats reserved for Scheduled Castes. The bulletin doesn't define a Karnataka SC candidate; we go by your domicile, so confirm with KEA if that differs from where your certificate was issued.
PwD: medical examination at KEA

PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only. Eligibility for benchmark disabilities follows the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (see the MCC PH notice on the KEA site). Every PwD candidate must attend a medical examination at KEA on the notified dates. If you're found not eligible under the Act, you'll be disqualified at any stage of admission.
PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only

PwD reservation applies to Karnataka candidates only, so you'd compete without PwD seats and need the General (UR) cut-off. The bulletin doesn't define 'Karnataka candidate'; we've used your domicile. Confirm with KEA.
In-service candidates

Detailed in-service guidelines, eligibility conditions and procedures will be published later, after KEA receives them from the Government/DME. Rule 9 of the MCI PG Medical Education Regulations, 2000 and in-service subject restrictions will apply. You pay the full fees and claim reimbursement from your department, and at admission you sign a bond to serve the Government for at least 10 years.
Parent-service route (clauses d, e, f and g)

You said a parent's service gives you a Karnataka route. Clauses d, e, f and g open Government seats, along with OPN, NRI and Others (Q) seats. GMP seats need clause b or c: only clause d lets you count the years you studied outside Karnataka during your parent's posting toward the 10 years, so under clause d GMP seats may open too. Check you meet every condition of your clause (see Other routes) and bring its certificates. Confirm with KEA.
Other routes: clauses d, e, f and g

Some candidates can count study outside Karnataka or don't need the 10 years. Clause d: children of a serving All India Service officer of the Karnataka cadre can count the years they studied outside Karnataka while the parent served outside Karnataka toward the 10 years under clause b or c. Clause e: children of an employee of the Union Government, or of a Union or Karnataka State Government undertaking or joint sector undertaking, if the parent declared a Karnataka home town on joining service, studied at least 10 years in Karnataka, and was or is liable to transfer anywhere in India. You can have passed the qualifying exam anywhere in India. The employer's certificate must show the parent is transferable, so if your parent has left service, confirm with KEA. Clause f: children of MPs elected from Karnataka, for years studied in New Delhi during the MP's tenure. Clause g: children of serving defence personnel or ex-servicemen who declared a Karnataka home town on joining; the qualifying exam can be from anywhere in India. These are routes to Government seats; the bulletin ties GMP seats only to clauses b and c. 'Children' means natural-born sons or daughters, not adopted children or grandchildren.
Hyderabad-Karnataka (Kalyana Karnataka) reservation, Article 371(j)

If you're a local person of the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, you can claim reservation under Article 371(j) with a certificate from the Assistant Commissioner (Annexure 8). Seats are first searched in General Merit (GM), then Hyderabad-Karnataka GM (GMH), then your category.
Christian and Muslim minority seats

Christian and Muslim candidates of clause b/c count as Karnataka religious minority candidates. After the Karnataka list is exhausted, leftover seats go to other eligible religious-minority candidates, including non-Karnataka ones. You need a religious minority certificate from the Tahsildar (Annexure 12).
Linguistic minority seats (Tamil, Telugu, Kodava, Tulu)

Linguistic minority seats are for Karnataka candidates whose mother tongue is Tamil, Telugu, Kodava or Tulu, and who studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in Karnataka, passing SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there. You need a linguistic minority certificate countersigned by the BEO or Deputy Director, PU (Annexure 9/10).
St. John's Medical College, Bengaluru

St. John's has four categories: (1) Roman Catholic religious nuns with SJMC-approved two-year rural service, (2) SJMC alumni with SJMC-approved two-year rural service, (3) Roman Catholic Christians, (4) general open merit. Categories 1 to 3 need their own certificates (Annexures 13 to 16). The bulletin lists no extra certificate for general open merit.
You must swear you hold no other PG admission

Every candidate signs the Annexure 7 affidavit, declaring they haven't taken PG admission in any college allotted by other exam-conducting bodies and haven't surrendered a seat in past NEET-PG/NEET-MDS or other state PG entrance counselling. The wording about which past exams count is unclear. If you can't truthfully declare this, check with KEA before applying. A false declaration means losing the seat and criminal proceedings.
Cancelled a PG seat or didn't join? 3-year bar

If, as a regular (non-in-service) candidate, you cancelled or surrendered a PG Medical/Dental seat after the last date of admissions, you're not eligible for a management quota or any other PG seat for three years. If you fail to join after allotment, the same three-year bar and disciplinary action apply, and this proviso appears to cover in-service candidates too.
Four types of seats

Seats are Government (G), Private (P), NRI (N) and Others (Q). Government seats are 50% of seats in government colleges (the other 50% go to All India Quota through MCC), 33% in private non-minority colleges, 20% in private minority colleges and 40% in private university colleges.
Private seats: GMP and OPN

In KPCF colleges, 42% of seats are private quota: half are GMP seats (GMPH in Hyderabad-Karnataka colleges) and half are OPN seats, filled on NEET-PG All India merit and open only to Indian citizens. In KRLMPCA and AMPCK colleges, 55% are private quota: 66% go to religious or linguistic minority candidates and the other 34% are split equally between GMP and OPN. In private universities, 40% are private quota.
NRI and Others (Q) seats
NRI seats are 15% of seats in KPCF, KRLMPCA, AMPCK and private university colleges. Others (Q) seats are 10% in KPCF, KRLMPCA and AMPCK colleges and 5% in private universities.
Reservation for Karnataka candidates only

SC/ST/OBC reservation applies only to Karnataka SC/ST/OBC candidates. Non-Karnataka candidates aren't eligible for reservations, though non-Karnataka Christian and Muslim candidates can get religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates.
SC internal reservation: SCA, SCB, SCC
Karnataka SC candidates need a caste certificate with SCA, SCB or SCC printed on it, and must enter its RD number when applying. Without it, you can't select seats reserved for Scheduled Castes.
How category seats are searched

For every option, the computer first looks for a General Merit (GM) seat, then your category seat (e.g. SC: GM, then SCG). Hyderabad-Karnataka candidates go through more steps (e.g. SCH: GM, GMH, SCG, then SCH), and PwD candidates through longer chains that include PWD seats. This improves your allotment as per the roster. The bulletin's text says GMH is checked after GM for every category, but its chart shows GMH only for Hyderabad-Karnataka candidates.
Your category can't be changed later
The caste/category, annual income and other reservation details you enter stay the same for verification and allotment. No change is allowed later for any reason.
Caste certificate forms

Caste or caste-income certificates come from the Tahsildar: Form-D for SC/ST, Form-E for Category-1, and Form-F for 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B. A married woman's certificate must be in her name with her husband's name and the spouse's income. Caste, income and 371(j) certificates must be in the name of the candidate and father.
PwD reservation
PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only, as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Every PwD candidate must attend the medical examination at KEA on the notified dates.
For General, 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B candidates. SC/ST/Category-1/PwD pay ₹750, non-Karnataka candidates ₹4,000, and NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates ₹7,000. Paid online through the payment gateway.
Registration fee depends on who you are
₹750 for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD candidates, ₹1,500 for General/2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹4,000 for non-Karnataka candidates and ₹7,000 for NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates.
Fees aren't refunded
Confirm you meet an eligibility clause before applying. The fee you pay won't be refunded for any reason.
Missed option entry before the mock? ₹750 to enter options
Eligible candidates who didn't enter options for the mock allotment can still enter options by registering and paying a non-refundable fee of ₹750.
Check the fee structure before choosing
The Government's seat matrix and fee structure are put on the KEA website. Check the fees, seat type and college location of each course before entering options, and discuss them with your parents.
SC/ST fee exemption (Karnataka candidates)

On Government seats (codes ending in G): annual income below ₹2.50 lakh, no fees; above ₹2.50 lakh and below ₹10 lakh, pay 50% of the tuition fee. On Private seats (codes ending in P), you pay the full fees. The bulletin isn't clear about an income of exactly ₹2.50 lakh; confirm with the concerned department.
Category-1 fee exemption (Karnataka candidates)

With annual income below ₹2.5 lakh: no fees for seats in government colleges. For Government-quota seats in private colleges, the government-college fee is deducted from what you pay. On Private seats (P), you pay the fees. Contact the concerned department about exemption and reimbursement criteria.
OBC: pay first, claim reimbursement
Other Backward Class candidates pay the fees to KEA and can apply to the Backward Classes Department for reimbursement after admission.
In-service candidates pay full fees
All in-service candidates pay the full fees and get reimbursed by their department as per deputation rules.
NRI sponsor payments
If an NRI sponsor pays your fees, follow the separate instructions on the KEA website for payment by an NRI sponsor.
NRI and Others (Q) seats: bank guarantee

Students on NRI and Others (Q) seats must give the college a bank guarantee for the balance course period, at admission or within the time the college allows. Otherwise the admission is cancelled or classes are suspended until it's provided.
One option list for Rounds 1 and 2

You enter options once. The same priority list is used for the first and second rounds, and you can't enter options again. After a round you can only delete or reorder them. You must declare before you can start option entry.
Enter options even where no seats are shown

Seats can come back from All India Quota surrenders, new intake approvals and new courses, and consequential vacancies arise during allotment. Enter every option you want in priority order, whatever the number of seats shown.
The mock allotment is only indicative

After option entry, a mock allotment shows the seat you might get, with college-, course- and category-wise mock cut-off ranks. You don't report to a college. Use it to add, delete or reorder options before the last date. The real allotment can differ because others change their options too.
No seat in the mock? Add more options
If you weren't allotted a seat in the mock allotment, check your options and add more you're interested in.
Options lock at the deadline
Enter your final options before the last date and time. You can't change them after that. Keep a printout of your final options.
You can't refuse a seat you opted for
Seats are allotted strictly by merit and your options. You can't claim ignorance or reject an allotted seat, so list only colleges and courses you'll actually join.
Verification slip needed

You can enter options only after online registration, payment and document verification at KEA, which gives you the documents verification slip. Clause a and clause y candidates are excused from attending verification, but the bulletin doesn't say how they get the slip. Confirm with KEA.
Two rounds, then mop-up and stray

Counselling has Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 (mop-up) and a stray vacancy round. Allotment follows merit, your options and the Government roster. Eligibility for each round is subject to MCC's conditions.
Every round
Every round is online, run by KEA
As per the NMC letter dated 24th July 2023, all rounds, including the stray vacancy round, are conducted online by KEA only.
Every round
Not reporting counts as seat blocking

If you're allotted a seat in any round, you must report to the college. Not reporting isn't treated as surrendering the seat: it's seat blocking, which attracts a penalty, and the Government may take legal action.
Every round
Getting your originals back

If you surrender a seat after results, originals are returned only after you pay the penalty. Candidates without a seat get originals back on request, collected in person with the original verification slip and ID card.
Every round
Pick one of four choices

After the Round 1 result, log in and select one of four choices. If you don't, or don't follow the prescribed procedure, your seat is cancelled automatically and you can't take part in further rounds.
Round 1
Choice 1: accept and quit counselling

You're fully satisfied and won't take part in later rounds. Pay the fees, submit originals, collect the admission order, report to the college by the last date, and update your joining status on the KEA portal. If you don't report back to KEA that you joined, your seat is cancelled even if you physically joined.
Round 1
Choice 1 but didn't join? Fees forfeited

If you pay and get the admission order but don't report by the last date, no extension is given. The allotment is cancelled, you aren't considered in later rounds, and the fees you paid are forfeited. Failing to produce originals or pay the fees also cancels the seat.
Round 1
Choice 2: keep the seat, try to upgrade

Pay the fees for your Round 1 seat and submit originals as scheduled. In Round 2 your current seat becomes your last option and only higher options are tried. If you get a higher one, your old seat is cancelled automatically. If not, you keep it. You can't choose between them, and you must take admission. No admission order is given at this stage.
Round 1
Choice 2: to keep your seat, delete higher options
All your higher options appear on screen. To keep your Round 1 seat, delete them all. Only keep options better than your seat.
Round 1
Choice 3: give up the seat, try again

Surrender your Round 1 seat and take part in Round 2 with your other options. You don't pay fees for the Round 1 seat, but you must submit originals or you can't take part. If Round 2 allots nothing, you have no seat.
Round 1
Choice 4: quit
You're not satisfied, have a seat elsewhere, and quit. Your seat is cancelled and you can't take part in later rounds.
Round 1
Round 2: originals are mandatory

To take part in Round 2, Choice 2 and Choice 3 candidates and those without a Round 1 seat must submit originals (verification slip, all originals including Annexures 1, 2 and 7, and one set of photocopies) as scheduled. Choice 2 candidates must also have paid the fees.
Round 2
Exited AIQ Round 2? You can join Round 2

If you were allotted a seat in All India Quota or Deemed University Round 2, didn't join and exited with the forfeiture clause, you can take part in Karnataka's Round 2 after depositing originals at KEA.
Round 2
Who can't take part in Round 2

Candidates who didn't enter options for Round 1, didn't exercise a choice, Choice 2 candidates who didn't pay or deposit originals, Choice 3 or unallotted candidates who didn't deposit originals, and Choice 1/2 candidates who cancelled or surrendered.
Round 2
Round 2: reorder, but no new options

You can reorder or delete options after confirming fees, but adding new options isn't permitted. Keep options even if no seats are shown, because vacancies arise during allotment. A vacancy that arises after your turn can't be claimed. Seats freed when Choice 2 candidates upgrade (virtual vacancies) go to the next candidate who kept that option.
Round 2
Round 2: no choices, joining is compulsory
There are no choices after Round 2. If you're allotted a seat, pay the fees (Choice 2 fees are adjusted) and report to the college by the last date. Taking admission is compulsory.
Round 2
Not joining a Round 2 seat means legal action
If you don't report to the college after a Round 2 allotment, legal action will be initiated against you.
Round 2
Got a better seat elsewhere? Surrender before Round 2
If you joined (Choice 1) or paid (Choice 2) and may take a seat from another board, surrender your seat to KEA on or before the last date for Round 2 option entry, so it goes to another candidate.
Round 2
Round 3: upgrade while admitted
As per recent High Court orders, candidates admitted to a Round 2 seat (or any KEA seat they joined) can take part in Round 3 for an upgrade. If you get nothing, your earlier seat stays confirmed.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
Who can take part in the mop-up

Candidates with no seat after KEA Round 2, and those who joined a KEA-allotted college. Not eligible: those allotted a seat who didn't exercise a choice in Round 1, didn't pay or didn't report, and anyone who joined a college through All India (including deemed university) counselling or any other board. This All India rule follows the MCC bulletin and is subject to any conditions set by the Government of India.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
Mop-up: enter options afresh
Only candidates holding the verification slip who deposit originals can enter options. Earlier options are ignored, so enter fresh ones, only for colleges and courses you'll join after checking fees.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
Mop-up: a new seat cancels the old one
If you're allotted a seat in this round, your earlier seat is cancelled automatically and you can't get it back. You must report to the newly allotted college.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
After mop-up: join and update KEA

There are no choices. Pay the fees (if not paid), report to the college by the last date on the admission order and update your details through your KEA login, or you lose the seat. Not reporting means legal action.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
Stray vacancy round eligibility

Only candidates who haven't been allotted any PG Medical/Dental seat by KEA in any round can take part. Those who reported to a college after MCC, deemed university or any other allotment in the three rounds, and those allotted a seat in MCC's stray vacancy round, aren't eligible.
Stray vacancy
Missing or fake originals
If any original certificate isn't produced during verification, or is false, concocted or a colour photocopy, you're disqualified from further allotment and liable for criminal prosecution.
Round 3 (Mop-up)
Admission is provisional

Join the college with the required undertakings by the due date on your admission order, or the seat is cancelled automatically. Admission stays subject to approval by the Government, apex bodies and the university.
False documents: seat cancelled and prosecution

If any information or document is false, fake or tampered, your seat is cancelled at any point during the course, all fees are forfeited, and KEA will start criminal proceedings. You may be debarred from future exams and counselling, and blacklisting and cancellation of your council registration may be recommended.
No changes after you apply

KEA won't edit any information you entered, including name, category, PwD status, qualification and date of birth, under any circumstances. Keep a hard copy of your application until counselling ends.
Certificates can be checked any time
KEA, DME, the Government and RGUHS can verify the authenticity of your certificates at any time, and KEA can withdraw any admission that doesn't meet the eligibility rules.
Attend verification yourself

You must attend document verification in person. No one can represent you. Verification takes time, and requests to be verified before your scheduled time won't be entertained, so plan your return journey. You can bring water, food and medicines.
Use your own mobile number and email
KEA sends updates only to the mobile number and email you registered. It isn't responsible if you miss information because of a wrong number. Check the KEA website often.
Don't share counselling content

Sharing any content of this counselling with others, including on WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter or other social media, breaches the non-disclosure agreement and can lead to penal action and cancellation of your candidature.
Beware of touts
Nobody can guarantee a PG seat through KEA. Seats go by NEET merit and your options. Report anyone claiming otherwise to keauthority-ka@nic.in.
MDS: your BDS aggregate is checked

The aggregate BDS percentage you gave in your NEET-MDS 2026 form is verified against your originals at admission. If it was used to break a rank tie and turns out to be wrong, your NEET-MDS 2026 candidature is cancelled.
The Rules prevail
The bulletin is subject to the Karnataka PG entrance test Rules, 2006 and government orders. If they differ, the Rules prevail, and the decision of the Government or Entrance Test Committee is final.
Appeal within 15 days

If you're aggrieved by an order of KEA's Executive Director, you can appeal within 15 days to the Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department, Government of Karnataka, whose decision is final. Disputes fall under the High Court of Karnataka.
3-year bar on new PG seats

If you're a regular (non-in-service) candidate and cancel or surrender a PG seat after the last date of admissions, you can't take a management quota or any other PG seat for three years. If you fail to join after allotment, the same bar and disciplinary action apply, and this appears to cover in-service candidates too.
You can't rejoin a seat you gave up
Whether you're a regular or in-service candidate, and whether you cancel before or after the last date, you aren't permitted to rejoin the cancelled or surrendered seat.
Surrender only through KEA or DME
Don't surrender a seat at the college. Surrender only at KEA, and after the last date of admission, only at the Directorate of Medical Education.
In-service candidates: recovery from salary

If an in-service candidate leaves the course, doesn't progress, doesn't finish on time, or fails to resume duty after deputation or at any time within ten years of finishing, the Government can recover everything spent (pay, allowances, stipend, DA, tuition fee) with penalty and interest from salary.
Originals are released only after the penalty
If you surrender after results, your original documents are returned only after you pay the penalty.
One year of compulsory service after PG

Everyone admitted to a PG Medical degree or diploma in a government, private or deemed college, under any quota, must do one year of compulsory service in a Government hospital in an urban area after finishing, under the Karnataka Compulsory Service Act, 2012. You get only temporary registration until you complete it. Candidates who already did compulsory rural service after MBBS are exempt.
Two sureties and originals held

The three-year undertaking needs two sureties with self-attested PAN and Aadhaar copies, and you and they are jointly and severally bound to pay the ₹50 lakh / ₹25 lakh penalty. Your original documents stay with the institution and are returned only after you pay any penalty.
In-service: 10 years of service
In-service candidates sign a bond at admission to serve the Government for at least ten years.
